note: Character-coordinate chart data. Every form here is matched by position over the Unicode code points of the text; nothing is tokenised by whitespace. A form is data, the scan is generic mechanics.

records.note: A segment boundary falls after the form. The form itself stays inside the segment.
Stripped from the edges of a value span before the span is recorded. Trimming only moves the span edges; the retained span is still exact.

A marker form is an eligible marker hit only when what follows it is one of these, or the end of the segment. This is a declared boundary cue, not a tokenisation: a value span may still cover many chunks.
A chunk is a maximal run of non-space characters. Chunks are used for two things only: deciding where a marker may attach, and offering nested mention starts. No role is read off a chunk count.
records.resolution_note: Among overlapping eligible marker hits the longest form is kept, and a closing form outranks an internal one at equal length. This removes only subsumption and spelling alternatives, so a longer case form is never shadowed by a shorter form it contains. Genuine class ambiguity — one marker form carrying several syntactic classes — is never resolved here and still yields competing readings (CONTRACT C6).
records.blocking_note: A marker hit is dropped when the chunk it ends is itself a declared form of one of these classes. 같은 and 동일한 end in characters that are also markers; without this the determiner would be split into a bogus value and a case marker. The test is character equality against declared forms, so it adds no guessing.
records.extension_note: A closing marker immediately followed by an internal marker takes the internal form into its own span instead of leaving it to the next value. 에서부터 therefore closes a value as an ablative rather than failing the boundary test and losing the origin altogether.

records.note: A marker form may also be a verb ending. A hit is dropped when the characters before it inside its own chunk end with a declared stem ending, so the adnominal -는 of 있는 is not read as a topic marker leaving the fragment 있 as a value. The inventory is declared, character-exact and admittedly incomplete; what it cannot catch leaves a clause unresolved rather than asserting a morpheme as a value.

rules.because: adnominal -는 / -은 on a verb or adjective stem is not a topic marker
the -이 of a nominalised verb is not a nominative marker

records.note: Where a frame binds a declared form class to a role, the form counts only if it begins a chunk and ends at a declared boundary form or at the predicate. A name that merely contains the form fails both tests, so a finding cannot be invented out of a substring.
